```rust
    # Ask the job table, not `$child`. A signal that lands between `"$@" &` and
    # `child=$!` runs this handler while `child` is still 0 (bash runs a trap
    # as soon as the `&` command returns, before the next assignment), so
    # relying on `$child` alone orphans a freshly forked restart-pause `sleep`
    # -- or the node itself -- which then outlives the wrapper. `jobs -p` also
    # lists `child` when it IS recorded, so it is only added when it is not.
    local pids
    pids="$(jobs -p)"
        case " ${pids//$'\n'/ } " in
            *" $child "*) ;;
            *) pids="$pids $child" ;;
        esac
    fi
    if [ -n "${pids// /}" ]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word splitting of a pid list is the point
        kill -TERM $pids 2>/dev/null || true
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        wait $pids 2>/dev/null || true
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [parcel-bundler/parcel](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel) (Revision: `59484858`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When building graph-traversal caches where lookup keys depend on both an overarching graph container and a sub-node (such as `BundleGraph` and `NamedBundle`), the compiler MUST use an outer `WeakMap<Graph, WeakMap<Node, Result>>` rather than composite string keys or direct node-level caches. If the operation traverses child nodes across parents, it MUST NEVER evaluate entry membership via redundant full-graph group scans inside loops.

**WHY**:
Flat composite key caching (`${graph.id}:${bundle.id}`) leaks memory when graphs or bundles are garbage collected, while direct attachment to bundles leads to cross-graph cache poisoning during incremental rebuilds. Redundant calls to `bundleGraph.getBundleGroupsContainingBundle(bundle).some(...)` inside inner loops transform graph linearization from $O(V + E)$ into $O(V \cdot G)$, which degrades compilation throughput exponentially when bundling thousands of split chunks in React Server Component (RSC) and micro-frontend graphs.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to any compiler pass, dependency resolver, or AST transform pipeline where an immutable or versioned graph structure undergoes repeated queries on behalf of individual graph elements across multiple worker threads or runtime injection plugins.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// packages/core/utils/src/import-map.js & applyRuntimes.js
import type {BundleGraph, NamedBundle} from '@parcel/types';

// Outer WeakMap anchored to the graph instance life-cycle
const importMapCache: WeakMap<
  BundleGraph<NamedBundle>,
  WeakMap<NamedBundle, {[string]: string}>
> = new WeakMap();

export function getImportMap(
  bundleGraph: BundleGraph<NamedBundle>,
  entryBundle: NamedBundle,
): {[string]: string} {
  let cache = importMapCache.get(bundleGraph);
  if (!cache) {
    cache = new WeakMap();
    importMapCache.set(bundleGraph, cache);
  }

  let cached = cache.get(entryBundle);
  if (cached) {
    return cached;
  }

  let mappings: {[string]: string} = {};
  for (let childBundle of bundleGraph.getChildBundles(entryBundle)) {
    bundleGraph.traverseBundles((bundle, _, actions) => {
      if (bundle === childBundle) {
        return;
      }
      if (isNewContext(bundle, bundleGraph)) {
        actions.skipChildren();
        return;
      }
      // Linear mapping insertion without redundant graph-group scanning
      mappings[bundle.publicId] = bundle.name;
    }, childBundle);
  }

  cache.set(entryBundle, mappings);
  return mappings;
}

function isNewContext(
  bundle: NamedBundle,
  bundleGraph: BundleGraph<NamedBundle>,
): boolean {
  let parents = bundleGraph.getParentBundles(bundle);
  // FAST-PATH: Determine context boundary strictly from local parent edges
  // DO NOT call getBundleGroupsContainingBundle in hot traversal path!
  return (
    parents.length === 0 ||
    parents.some(parent => parent.env.context !== bundle.env.context)
  );
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:

```javascript
  const key = bundleGraph.id + ':' + entryBundle.id;
  if (leakyCache.has(key)) return leakyCache.get(key);

  let mappings = {};
  for (let child of bundleGraph.getChildBundles(entryBundle)) {
    bundleGraph.traverseBundles((bundle) => {
      // PERFORMANCE BOMB: Scanning all groups across graph on EVERY inner step
      let isInEntryGroup = bundleGraph
        .getBundleGroupsContainingBundle(bundle)
        .some(g => bundleGraph.isEntryBundleGroup(g));
      if (isInEntryGroup) {
        // ...
      }
    }, child);
  }
  leakyCache.set(key, mappings);
  return mappings;
}
```

```javascript
it('releases graph and bundle references when out of scope without retention', async () => {
  let graph = createMockBundleGraph();
  let bundle = createMockBundle();
  getImportMap(graph, bundle);
  
  let refGraph = new WeakRef(graph);
  let refBundle = new WeakRef(bundle);

  bundle = null;
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [parcel-bundler/parcel](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel) (Revision: `59484858`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When dynamic module loaders execute mixed-environment compilation assets (e.g., Client Components vs. Server Components vs. Static Packagers in Node VM contexts), the system MUST pass the target environment context directly into the module loader resolution hook. It MUST NOT alias or substitute standard client libraries (`react`, `react-dom`) with single-environment resolutions when packaging multi-tier bundles.

**WHY**:
Server component compilation targets must separate `react-server` environments from browser/client execution environments. If a static packager imports DOM execution utilities (such as `preload` or DOM-specific rendering primitives) under an aliased server context or binds `ReactDOM` to the `react` root entrypoint, runtime failure occurs instantly with `ReactDOM.preload is not a function` or unresolved export descriptors under edge/Node runtimes.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Universal to all meta-framework compilers, bundlers, and server-side packagers that synthesize React Server Components, Next.js App Router equivalents, or multi-target workers (browser, node, edge, and workers) from a unified dependency graph.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// packages/packagers/react-static/src/ReactStaticPackager.js
// Explicitly bifurcate module acquisition using accurate target environments:
let React = loadModule('react', __filename, 'react-client');
let ReactDOM = loadModule('react-dom', __filename, 'react-server');
let {createFromReadableStream} = loadModule(
  'react-server-dom-parcel/client.edge',
  __filename,
  'react-client',
);

function Resources({referencedBundles}) {
  let resources = [];
  for (let b of referencedBundles) {
    if (b.type === 'css') {
      let href = urlJoin(b.target.publicUrl, b.name);

      // Invariant: Preload stylesheet hints directly via react-dom server API
      // without waiting for the client tree hydration/mount phase.
      ReactDOM.preload(href, {as: 'style'});
      resources.push(
        React.createElement('link', {
          key: b.id,
          rel: 'stylesheet',
          href,
          precedence: 'default',
        }),
      );
    } else if (b.type === 'js' && b.env.isBrowser()) {
      resources.push(
        React.createElement('script', {
          key: b.id,
          type: 'module',
          async: true,
          src: urlJoin(b.target.publicUrl, b.name),
        }),
      );
    }
  }
  return resources;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Erroneously binding react-dom to 'react' module specifier,
// or executing DOM preload operations on a raw 'react-client' bundle without DOM bindings.
let React = loadModule('react', __filename, 'react-client');
let ReactDOM = loadModule('react', __filename, 'react-server'); // BUG: Points to react, NOT react-dom!

// Results in:
// TypeError: ReactDOM.preload is not a function
ReactDOM.preload(href, {as: 'style'});
```

When an autonomous build engine catches lower-level compiler failures containing diagnostics with source code locations, it MUST normalize and populate missing source frames (`codeFrame.code`) at the boundary throw site before surfacing errors to external consumers or reporters. Furthermore, it MUST read source files non-destructively, swallow filesystem read errors gracefully (e.g., deleted files during watch mode), and NEVER mutate original diagnostic objects in-place.

**WHY**:
Downstream API consumers (LSP servers, CI formatters, dev-server error overlays) inspect `error.diagnostics[i].codeFrames[j].code` directly. If the engine defers file reading exclusively to terminal CLI reporters (e.g., `prettyDiagnostic()`), programmatic API callers receive `undefined` code frames and crash or produce unhelpful stack traces without source context. Mutating the error object directly breaks idempotency when error instances are passed across multiple event listeners or plugin reporters.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to all diagnostic reporting boundaries, compilers, transpilers, language servers, and task runners handling source-mapped compilation errors.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// packages/core/diagnostic/src/diagnostic.js
import type {Diagnostic, FileSystem} from '@parcel/types';
import path from 'path';

export async function normalizeCodeFrames(
  diagnostics: Array<Diagnostic>,
  readFile: (filePath: string) => Promise<string>,
  projectRoot?: string,
): Promise<Array<Diagnostic>> {
  return Promise.all(
    diagnostics.map(async (diagnostic) => {
      if (!diagnostic.codeFrames || diagnostic.codeFrames.length === 0) {
        return diagnostic;
      }

      let codeFrames = await Promise.all(
        diagnostic.codeFrames.map(async (codeFrame) => {
          // If code is already populated or no file path exists, preserve untouched
          if (codeFrame.code != null || !codeFrame.filePath) {
            return codeFrame;
          }

          let resolvedPath = projectRoot
            ? path.resolve(projectRoot, codeFrame.filePath)
            : codeFrame.filePath;

          try {
            let code = await readFile(resolvedPath);
            // Return immutable clone with normalized code string
            return {
              ...codeFrame,
              code,
            };
          } catch (err) {
            // Non-destructive degradation: Swallow read error and keep code undefined
            return codeFrame;
          }
        }),
      );

      return {
        ...diagnostic,
        codeFrames,
      };
    }),
  );
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Mutating diagnostic in-place, throwing on missing disk assets,
// or leaving code undefined for programmatic API consumers.
function badNormalize(diagnostics) {
  for (let diag of diagnostics) {
    for (let frame of diag.codeFrames) {
      if (!frame.code) {
        // BUG 1: In-place mutation
        // BUG 2: Synchronous crash if file was deleted during watch build
        frame.code = fs.readFileSync(frame.filePath, 'utf8');
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Execute an automated unit test verifying non-mutation, missing-file survival, and code frame population:
```javascript
it('normalizes missing code frames non-destructively and tolerates missing files', async () => {
  let originalDiagnostics = [{
    message: 'Syntax error',
    codeFrames: [{filePath: '/virtual/deleted.js', code: undefined}],
  }];
  
  let fs = {
    readFile: async (p) => {
      if (p === '/virtual/deleted.js') {
        let err = new Error('ENOENT');
        err.code = 'ENOENT';
        throw err;
      }
      return 'const x = 1;';
    }
  };

  let normalized = await normalizeCodeFrames(originalDiagnostics, fs.readFile);
  expect(normalized).to.not.equal(originalDiagnostics);
  expect(normalized[0].codeFrames[0].code).to.be.undefined;
});
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [alyssaxuu/later](https://github.com/alyssaxuu/later) (Revision: `26e79369`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When using `NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents` (or similar global event hooks in other frameworks), the monitor object **MUST** be stored in a strong reference variable within a dedicated wrapper class. The wrapper **MUST** implement a `deinit` or explicit `stop()` method that calls `NSEvent.removeMonitor` and nils the reference. You **MUST NOT** create the monitor in a local scope or discard the returned object, as the system will immediately invalidate the monitor if the reference is lost, or leak memory if not explicitly removed.

**WHY**:
`NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents` returns an opaque object that the system uses to track the subscription. If this object is not retained, the monitor stops working immediately (silent failure). If it is retained but never removed, it causes a memory leak and continues to fire callbacks even after the owning view/controller is destroyed, leading to "zombie" event handlers that may crash the app if they reference deallocated UI elements.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any macOS/iOS application using global event monitoring (keyboard shortcuts, mouse movements, app activation changes) via Cocoa/AppKit.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```swift
import Cocoa

class SafeEventMonitor {
    private var monitor: AnyObject?
    private let mask: NSEvent.EventTypeMask
    private let handler: (NSEvent?) -> Void

    init(mask: NSEvent.EventTypeMask, handler: @escaping (NSEvent?) -> Void) {
        self.mask = mask
        self.handler = handler
    }

    func start() {
        // Retain the monitor object
        monitor = NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents(matching: mask, handler: handler)
    }

    func stop() {
        if let monitor = monitor {
            NSEvent.removeMonitor(monitor)
            self.monitor = nil
        }
    }

    deinit {
        stop()
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```swift
// ANTI-PATTERN: Silent Failure
func setupGlobalShortcut() {
    // The returned object is not stored. The monitor is immediately invalid.
    _ = NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown) { event in
        print("This will never print")
    }
}

// ANTI-PATTERN: Memory Leak / Zombie Handler
var globalMonitor: AnyObject?

func setupLeakyShortcut() {
    globalMonitor = NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown) { event in
        // If the view controller is deallocated, this closure might capture
        // weak references that are now nil, or strong references that prevent deallocation.
        self.someUIElement.update() 
    }
    // No stop() method called when view disappears.
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
1.  **Static Analysis**: Lint rule to ensure `NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents` return value is assigned to a property.
2.  **Unit Test**: Create a `SafeEventMonitor`, start it, simulate an event, stop it, and assert that no further events are received.
3.  **Memory Profiling**: Use Instruments (Leaks) to verify that starting and stopping the monitor multiple times does not increase the baseline memory footprint.

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [alyssaxuu/later](https://github.com/alyssaxuu/later) (Revision: `26e79369`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When saving a "workspace" or "session" of running applications, you **MUST** identify applications by their `bundleIdentifier` (String) rather than their `processIdentifier` (Int) or `NSRunningApplication` object reference. You **MUST** filter out the current application's bundle ID and system-critical bundle IDs (e.g., `com.apple.dock`, `com.apple.finder`) before saving.

**WHY**:
`processIdentifier` is ephemeral and changes every time an app restarts. `NSRunningApplication` objects are not serializable and become invalid if the app terminates. `bundleIdentifier` is stable across restarts and is the canonical key for relaunching an app via `NSWorkspace`. Failing to filter system apps leads to crashes or unwanted behavior when trying to "restore" the Dock or Finder.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any application that needs to persist, serialize, or restore a list of running applications (e.g., session managers, window managers, productivity tools).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```swift
import AppKit

struct SessionSnapshot: Codable {
    let bundleIDs: [String]
    let timestamp: Date
}

func captureCurrentSession() -> SessionSnapshot {
    let currentBundleID = Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier
    let systemApps: Set<String> = [
        "com.apple.dock",
        "com.apple.finder",
        "com.apple.systempreferences",
        "com.apple.notificationcenterui"
    ]
    
    let runningApps = NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications
    let userApps = runningApps
        .filter { app in
            guard let bundleID = app.bundleIdentifier else { return false }
            return bundleID != currentBundleID && !systemApps.contains(bundleID)
        }
        .map { $0.bundleIdentifier! }
    
    return SessionSnapshot(bundleIDs: userApps, timestamp: Date())
}

func restoreSession(_ snapshot: SessionSnapshot) {
    for bundleID in snapshot.bundleIDs {
        if let url = NSWorkspace.shared.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier: bundleID) {
            NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at: url, configuration: NSWorkspace.OpenConfiguration())
        }
    }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```swift
// ANTI-PATTERN: Ephemeral State
struct BadSession {
    let pids: [Int] // PIDs change on restart
}

func badCapture() -> BadSession {
    let pids = NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications.map { $0.processIdentifier }
    return BadSession(pids: pids)
}

// ANTI-PATTERN: Unfiltered System Apps
func badRestore() {
    // Trying to "restore" the Dock or Finder can cause UI glitches or permission errors
    for app in savedApps {
        if app.bundleIdentifier == "com.apple.dock" {
            // Undefined behavior or crash
        }
    }
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
1.  **Unit Test**: Mock `NSWorkspace.shared.runningApplications` to return a list including system apps and the current app. Assert that `captureCurrentSession()` excludes them.
2.  **Integration Test**: Save a session, quit all apps, restore the session, and assert that the expected apps are running and system apps are unaffected.

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [testing-library/dom-testing-library](https://github.com/testing-library/dom-testing-library) (Revision: `6049cc0b`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When programmatically mutating a DOM node or object property whose setter has been overridden by a reactive framework (e.g., React, Vue, Angular tracking synthetic input events via internal trackers), you MUST traverse the prototype chain via `Object.getPrototypeOf()` to retrieve and invoke the original prototype property descriptor setter (`HTMLInputElement.prototype`), rather than assigning directly to `element[property]`.

**WHY**:
Frameworks like React patch property descriptors (specifically `value`, `checked`) on the target element instance to intercept user inputs and reconcile virtual DOM state. A direct property assignment (`element.value = "foo"`) merely triggers the framework's internal tracker without changing the underlying DOM state properly, or fails to fire necessary tracker flags when a subsequent `change` or `input` event is dispatched. Bypassing the immediate descriptor ensures the true underlying C++/host-level property mutation executes.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any library, end-to-end framework, testing harness, or browser extension that programmatically changes native DOM element properties (`value`, `checked`, `files`) before dispatching synthetic DOM events (`input`, `change`).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// Complete production pattern from src/events.js
function setNativeValue(element, value) {
  // 1. Check for setter on current instance
  const {set: valueSetter} = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(element, 'value') || {}
  
  // 2. Extract setter from the prototype (e.g., HTMLInputElement.prototype)
  const prototype = Object.getPrototypeOf(element)
  const {set: prototypeValueSetter} = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(prototype, 'value') || {}

  // 3. If instance hijacked the setter, invoke the prototype's raw setter
  if (prototypeValueSetter && valueSetter !== prototypeValueSetter) {
    prototypeValueSetter.call(element, value)
  } else if (valueSetter) {
    valueSetter.call(element, value)
  } else {
    throw new Error('The given element does not have a value setter')
  }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// ANTI-PATTERN: NEVER mutate properties directly when simulating native input
function naiveSetValue(element, value) {
  // FAILS: React 16+ tracks input value changes via setter wrapping.
  // Direct assignment makes React consider the input "not dirty", swallowing synthetic events!
  element.value = value;
  element.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Mount an input component in a simulated React test harness that records state updates via `onChange`. Assert that dispatching `fireEvent.change(input, {target: {value: 'abc'}})` triggers the state update handler and updates the rendered DOM node without throwing warnings.

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [testing-library/dom-testing-library](https://github.com/testing-library/dom-testing-library) (Revision: `6049cc0b`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When implementing an asynchronous polling loop driven by simulated or fake timers (e.g., `jest.advanceTimersByTime()`), you MUST check the loop's `finished` / `timedOut` sentinel flag immediately *after* timer advancement and *before* invoking the worker callback.

**WHY**:
Timer advancement routines (`advanceTimersByTime`) trigger pending macro-tasks synchronously. If the allotted time budget expires inside that advancement window, the timeout handler marks the task complete/rejected. If the polling loop immediately proceeds to invoke the worker callback without verifying the termination condition, the callback executes in an expired, poisoned context. This causes unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and React `act()` boundary leaks.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any async utility, test runner, wait-condition engine (`waitFor`, `poll`, `retryUntil`), or reconciliation worker operating in an environment supporting fake/virtualized system clocks.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// Complete production pattern adapted from src/wait-for.js
async function runPollingLoopWithFakeTimers({
  checkCallback,
  timeoutMs,
  intervalMs,
  advanceTimers,
}) {
  let finished = false
  let timedOut = false

  const timerId = setTimeout(() => {
    timedOut = true
    finished = true
  }, timeoutMs)

  try {
    while (!finished) {
      // Advance virtual clock, flushing queued timers
      advanceTimers(intervalMs)

      // CRITICAL GUARD: Check termination IMMEDIATELY after clock advancement.
      // Clock advancement might have fired the timeout handler synchronously!
      if (finished) {
        break
      }

      // Safe to run callback; clock has not expired
      checkCallback()
    }
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timerId)
  }

  if (timedOut) {
    throw new Error(`Timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms.`)
  }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Executing work after timer jump without checking termination
while (!finished) {
  advanceTimers(intervalMs); // Synchronously triggers timeout handler -> finished = true!
  
  // DEFECT: Callback runs even though the operation timed out!
  // Leaks execution outside the async boundary.
  checkCallback(); 

  if (finished) {
    break;
  }
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Configure fake timers with `jest.useFakeTimers()`. Execute a `waitFor` loop where the callback always throws and the timeout is `100ms` with an interval of `50ms`. Assert via an asynchronous tracking spy that when the assertion rejects with a timeout, the callback is NOT invoked after the timeout rejection resolves.

**RULE**:
When parsing environment configuration flags in code that executes across multiple JavaScript execution realms (Node.js CLI, Jest JSDOM runner, Browser bundlers, Edge workers), you MUST NOT use bare `process.env` access or assume `process.env[KEY]` contains valid JSON. You MUST wrap JSON deserialization in a `try/catch` and explicitly assert primitive types (`typeof result === 'boolean'`), defaulting safely without throwing exceptions on malformed input.

**WHY**:
Tooling environments inject stubbed or mock `process` globals into browser bundles (via Webpack, Vite, Rollup, or JSDOM). If an environment variable is defined as an empty string (`""`), a non-JSON string (`"true"` vs `"1"`), or an unparseable object, `JSON.parse(process?.env?.KEY)` throws an uncaught syntax exception. Reverting to host detection must be resilient to partially shimmed host objects where `process` exists but `process.versions` is undefined.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Configuration modules, logging layers, and CLI tools targeting isomorphic / cross-realm execution environments.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```javascript
// Extracted and fortified from src/pretty-dom.js
const shouldHighlight = () => {
  let colors
  try {
    // Defensively access process and parse only if defined
    if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process?.env?.COLORS !== undefined) {
      colors = JSON.parse(process.env.COLORS)
    }
  } catch {
    // Swallowing JSON parse error is safe here: 
    // malformed env vars must fall back gracefully to environment detection.
  }

  if (typeof colors === 'boolean') {
    return colors
  }

  // Multi-tier defensive host detection
  return (
    typeof process !== 'undefined' &&
    process.versions !== undefined &&
    process.versions.node !== undefined
  )
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```javascript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Fragile assumption of process presence and JSON formatting
const shouldHighlightBad = () => {
  // THROWS: SyntaxError: Unexpected token in JSON at position 0 if COLORS="true" (without quotes)
  // CRASHES: TypeError if running in browser bundle where process is undefined!
  return JSON.parse(process.env.COLORS) || Boolean(process.versions.node);
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Execute unit tests in 3 states: (1) `process.env.COLORS = ''`, (2) `process.env.COLORS = '{}'`, (3) `delete process.versions.node`. Verify that the function returns deterministic boolean outputs without throwing `SyntaxError` or `TypeError`.

**RULE**:
When computing an inverted or negated subset over a bounded alphabet (e.g., regex negated character sets `[^...]`), you MUST collect excluded values into a hashed lookup table (`Set<T>`) and construct the complement by filtering the authorized domain universe in a single forward pass. You MUST NOT compute set negation by mutating a mutable array using `.indexOf()` and `.splice()` in a loop.

**WHY**:
Inverting a collection via `array.indexOf(item)` and conditional `array.splice(index, 1)` / `array.push(item)` causes algorithmic instability:
- If duplicate entries or non-alphabet characters (such as regex range dashes `-` or case-folded characters) are introduced into the exclusion list, iterating over target ranges causes duplicate deletions, state desynchronization, and silent re-insertion of forbidden symbols.
- Array mutation inside an unindexed loop incurs $O(N \cdot M)$ time complexity, leading to microtask stalls during regex compilation.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Lexers, parsers, regex generators, permission masking systems, character set normalizers, and filter evaluation passes.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
/**
 * Safely inverts an excluded character code array against standard ASCII printable ranges.
 * Guaranteed O(U) time where U is the universe size, immune to duplicate or out-of-band exclusions.
 */
export function buildNegatedAsciiRanges(rawExcludedCodes: readonly number[]): number[] {
  const excludedSet = new Set<number>(rawExcludedCodes);
  const result: number[] = [];

  // Define authorized candidate universe partitions
  const ASCII_UNIVERSE_RANGES: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [
    [48, 57],   // 0-9
    [65, 90],   // A-Z
    [97, 122],  // a-z
  ];

  for (const [rangeStart, rangeEnd] of ASCII_UNIVERSE_RANGES) {
    for (let code = rangeStart; code <= rangeEnd; code++) {
      if (!excludedSet.has(code)) {
        result.push(code);
      }
    }
  }

  return result;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// CRITICAL DEFECT: Splice-toggle logic.
// If code exists, it deletes it. If it doesn't, it pushes it.
// Traps:
// 1. If 'rawCodes' contains out-of-range symbols (e.g. ASCII 45 '-'), they bypass range loops and persist.
// 2. If 'rawCodes' contains duplicates (case-folding /i), splice removes on hit 1, then push re-adds on hit 2!
function brokenInvert(rangeCodes: number[]): void {
  for (let i = 48; i <= 57; i++) {
    const index = rangeCodes.indexOf(i);
    if (index > -1) {
      rangeCodes.splice(index, 1);
      continue;
    }
    rangeCodes.push(i); // Re-adds excluded characters if duplicate hits occurred
  }
}
```

```typescript
test('verify inverted set contains zero excluded elements across boundary conditions', () => {
  const testExclusions = [45, 48, 48, 65, 90, 97, 122]; // Includes '-' (45) and duplicate '0' (48)
  const result = buildNegatedAsciiRanges(testExclusions);

  for (const excluded of testExclusions) {
    expect(result).not.toContain(excluded);
  }
  expect(result.every(code => 
    (code >= 48 && code <= 57) ||

  )).toBe(true);
```

**RULE**:
Any generator, parser, or template expansion function that accepts an externally controlled quantifier, count, or repetition factor MUST validate the count against safe engine-specific operational limits before invoking memory-allocating engine primitives (`Array.from({ length })`, `new Array(count)`, `String.prototype.repeat(count)`). Functions MUST catch or intercept out-of-bound inputs and throw domain-specific, typed exceptions rather than allowing uncaught native V8 runtime errors (`RangeError: Invalid array length` or `RangeError: Invalid string length`).

**WHY**:
Native V8/JavaScript engine `RangeError` exceptions bypass standard application-level domain error handling boundaries. In production systems utilizing dynamic mock templates (e.g., `faker.helpers.fake()`) or untrusted schema specifications, an unvalidated quantifier such as `x{4294967296}` instantly crashes the process or aborts active worker threads via an unhandled rejection, creating an exploitable Denial of Service (DoS) attack surface.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All array generators, string duplication routines, collection multipliers, parser quantifiers, and serialization repeaters.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
export class FakerError extends Error {
  public override readonly name = 'FakerError';
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    Object.setPrototypeOf(this, new.target.prototype);
  }
}

// Engine boundary constants (Node.js / V8 max string and safe allocation caps)
const MAX_SAFE_REPEAT_COUNT = 10_000_000; // Operational safety ceiling
const MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH_LIMIT = 4_294_967_295; // 2^32 - 1 (ECMA-262 array limit)

export function safeRepeat(target: string, repetitions: number): string {
  if (!Number.isFinite(repetitions) || repetitions < 0) {
    throw new FakerError(`Repetitions must be a non-negative finite number, received: ${repetitions}`);
  }

  if (repetitions > MAX_SAFE_REPEAT_COUNT) {
    throw new FakerError(
      `Repetition count ${repetitions} exceeds the maximum safe operational limit (${MAX_SAFE_REPEAT_COUNT})`
    );
  }

  try {
    return target.repeat(repetitions);
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    if (error instanceof RangeError) {
      throw new FakerError(`Failed to repeat string: allocation exceeded engine memory limits.`);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

export function safeMultiple<T>(generator: () => T, count: number): T[] {
  if (!Number.isInteger(count) || count < 0 || count >= MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH_LIMIT) {
    throw new FakerError(`Count must be an integer between 0 and 2^32 - 2, received: ${count}`);
  }

  // Pre-allocation cap check to prevent heap exhaustion DoS
  const MAX_HEAP_ALLOCATION = 1_000_000;
  if (count > MAX_HEAP_ALLOCATION) {
    throw new FakerError(`Requested array size ${count} exceeds single-operation heap threshold.`);
  }

  const result = new Array<T>(count);
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    result[i] = generator();
  }
  return result;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// CRITICAL FLAW: Trusting input count directly in engine allocators.
// An input of count = 2**32 throws native RangeError: Invalid array length.
// An input of 'a'.repeat(2**31) throws native RangeError: Invalid string length.
export function unsafeMultiple<T>(method: () => T, count: number): T[] {
  // Vulnerable to unhandled V8 RangeError
  return Array.from({ length: count }, method);
}

export function unsafeRegexRepeat(pattern: string, token: RegExpExecArray, count: number): string {
  // Vulnerable to DoS when token[1] is repeated count times without upper-bound guards
  return pattern.slice(0, token.index) + token[1].repeat(count) + pattern.slice(token.index + token[0].length);
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

describe('boundary enforcement for repetition primitives', () => {
  it('intercepts oversized array count and throws FakerError', () => {
    expect(() => safeMultiple(() => 1, 4_294_967_296)).toThrowError(FakerError);
    expect(() => safeMultiple(() => 1, -1)).toThrowError(FakerError);
  });

  it('intercepts oversized string repetition and throws FakerError', () => {
    expect(() => safeRepeat('x', 4_294_967_296)).toThrowError(FakerError);
  });
});
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [fallow-rs/fallow](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow) (Revision: `f6700ad1`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
A static mutation testing generator MUST NOT emit a mutant for a branch condition, `case` label, or predicate expression when the branch's consequent block and the system's terminal fallback (`default`, `else`, or implicit exit) execute strictly identical instructions and terminate with an unconditional transfer of control (`return`, `throw`, unlabeled `break`/`continue`).

**WHY**:
Generating a mutant that swaps one value for another when both target blocks yield the exact same side-effects and control transfer produces an *equivalent mutant*. No suite of test inputs can distinguish the original program from the mutant, causing false negatives in mutation scores, pipeline thrashing, and wasted LLM/agent compute cycles attempting to write tests for unkillable variants.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Static analysis mutation engines, fuzzers, and AST transformation engines for JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, C++, and Go where control-flow AST nodes contain multiple branches targeting identical terminal basic blocks.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```rust
// Verified pattern from crates/mutation/src/collect.rs
use oxc_ast::ast::{Expression, Statement, SwitchCase};
use oxc_span::{GetSpan, Span};

#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum LabelValue<'a> {
    String(&'a str),
    Boolean(bool),
    Other,
}

pub fn label_value<'a>(test: &Expression<'a>) -> Option<LabelValue<'a>> {
    match test {
        Expression::StringLiteral(it) => Some(LabelValue::String(it.value.as_str())),
        Expression::BooleanLiteral(it) => Some(LabelValue::Boolean(it.value)),
        Expression::NumericLiteral(_) | Expression::NullLiteral(_) => Some(LabelValue::Other),
        _ => None,
    }
}

pub fn mutated_value(value: &LabelValue<'_>) -> Option<LabelValue<'static>> {
    match value {
        LabelValue::String("") => Some(LabelValue::String("fallow")),
        LabelValue::String(_) => Some(LabelValue::String("")),
        LabelValue::Boolean(flag) => Some(LabelValue::Boolean(!flag)),
        LabelValue::Other => None,
    }
}

pub fn is_exit(statement: &Statement<'_>) -> bool {
    match statement {
        Statement::ReturnStatement(_) | Statement::ThrowStatement(_) => true,
        Statement::BreakStatement(it) => it.label.is_none(),
        Statement::ContinueStatement(it) => it.label.is_none(),
        _ => false,
    }
}

pub fn exiting_body<'s>(source: &'s str, case: &SwitchCase<'_>) -> Option<&'s str> {
    let first = case.consequent.first()?;
    let last = case.consequent.last()?;
    if !is_exit(last) {
        return None;
    }
    source.get(first.span().start as usize..last.span().end as usize)
}

pub fn should_skip_case_mutant(
    source: &str,
    target_case: &SwitchCase<'_>,
    default_case: &SwitchCase<'_>,
    all_cases: &[SwitchCase<'_>],
) -> bool {
    // 1. Both the candidate clause and default clause must terminate unconditionally
    let (Some(target_body), Some(default_body)) = (
        exiting_body(source, target_case),
        exiting_body(source, default_case),
    ) else {
        return false;
    };

    // 2. Clause bodies must have identical textual execution
    if target_body.trim() != default_body.trim() {
        return false;
    }

    // 3. Every case test must resolve to a literal expression
    let Some(target_expr) = &target_case.test else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(orig_val) = label_value(target_expr) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(mut_val) = mutated_value(&orig_val) else {
        return false;
    };

    // 4. No other case label must already match the original or mutated value
    let mut collisions = 0;
    for case in all_cases {
        if let Some(test_expr) = &case.test {
            if let Some(val) = label_value(test_expr) {
                if val == orig_val || val == mut_val {
                    collisions += 1;
                }
            } else {
                return false; // Dynamic expression present; cannot guarantee equivalence
            }
        }
    }

    // Exactly 1 collision (the original case statement itself) confirms mutation equivalence
    collisions == 1
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:

**RULE**:
All production and development container definitions (`Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dev`) MUST pin every base image using its immutable cryptographic multi-arch index digest (`@sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}`) alongside human-readable semantic tags, and MUST install node-based ecosystem tooling exclusively from committed lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`) via `--prefix` or isolated staging paths with `--ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`.

**WHY**:
Floating tags (e.g., `FROM rust:1.99.0-bookworm` or `FROM node:26-bookworm-slim`) are mutable references. Upstream registry rebuilds, base Debian patch updates, or architecture-specific tag shifts break reproducible builds, introduce unvetted vulnerabilities, invalidate deterministic compiler outputs, and expose CI runners to upstream registry compromises. Installing global packages via `npm install -g <pkg>@<ver>` bypasses integrity SHA-512 hashes and executes unvetted post-install hooks.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All Dockerfiles, container staging configurations, DevContainers, and packaging definitions across CI/CD systems, monorepos, and agent runners.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```dockerfile

FROM debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:7c7b2c966bc9ee8cedfeef67e0e279108992c77681fa595db4a9d65c06ccc587 AS download

ARG FALLOW_VERSION=3.34.1
ARG TARGETARCH

# Hardcoded cryptographic asset hashes per architecture
RUN set -eux; \
  case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
    amd64) \
      asset="fallow-linux-x64-musl"; \
      sha256="6f574e3e137e30d781fe10c23f99150afc84d4d87d3734f8b2a4ed9ab25e2fa4"; \
      ;; \
    arm64) \
      asset="fallow-linux-arm64-musl"; \
      sha256="a6a4fd6197456ac561b74fbfed7d84d22b40888eca729a3ce0e708ea6fca8a3f"; \
      ;; \
    *) \
      echo "unsupported TARGETARCH: ${TARGETARCH}" >&2; \
      exit 1; \
      ;; \
  esac; \
  curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 \
    "https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/releases/download/v${FALLOW_VERSION}/${asset}" -o /usr/local/bin/fallow; \
  echo "${sha256}  /usr/local/bin/fallow" | sha256sum -c -; \
  chmod +x /usr/local/bin/fallow

FROM node:26-bookworm-slim@sha256:298992629d69bbd5b2b03ad57094d8e4fcb3a8eeb7c4e25d29de656519568913 AS runtime

# Install corepack pinned via dedicated workspace lockfile and integrity hash
COPY tools/corepack/package.json tools/corepack/package-lock.json /opt/corepack/

RUN apt-get update \
  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates git \
  && npm ci --prefix /opt/corepack --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund \
  && ln -sf /opt/corepack/node_modules/corepack/dist/corepack.js /usr/local/bin/corepack \
  && corepack enable --install-directory /usr/local/bin \
  && npm cache clean --force \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

**RULE**:
Autonomous agent execution pre-tool interception hooks MUST inspect command payloads via quote-aware, POSIX-compliant lexical tokenization (`shlex`) rather than raw regular expressions, and MUST deny unbounded workspace-wide test or build execution commands lacking terminal pagers, output file redirects, or explicit local build bin overrides.

**WHY**:
Unbounded CLI runs (such as `cargo test --workspace` or `npm test`) dump hundreds of kilobytes of unstructured terminal output into the agent's context window. This triggers context window exhaustion, microtask starvation, token budget burnout, and model amnesia. Furthermore, simple string matching (e.g. searching for `fallow` or `git commit`) yields false positives on heredocs, test strings, or `echo` statements, while missing malicious chained executions like `VAR=1 && cargo test`.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Pre-execution hooks, MCP server command boundaries, and agent supervisor runtime environments (such as Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenAI agent wrappers).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
# Verified pattern from .claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.py
import json
import os
import re
import shlex
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SEPARATORS = {";", "&&", "||", "|", "&", "|&"}
CARGO_NOISY = {"build", "test", "clippy", "doc"}
BOUNDING_PAGERS = {"tail", "head", "less", "more", "wc", "grep", "rg"}
ENV_ASSIGN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=")

def command_positions(command: str) -> list[list[str]] | None:
    """Split command into argv segments aware of shell quoting."""
    try:
        tokens = shlex.split(command, posix=True)
    except ValueError:
        return None  # Unbalanced quotes; fail safe

    segments: list[list[str]] = []
    current: list[str] = []
    for token in tokens:
        if token in SEPARATORS:
            if current:
                segments.append(current)
                current = []
        else:
            current.append(token)
    if current:
        segments.append(current)

    return [strip_env(seg) for seg in segments if seg]

def strip_env(segment: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    index = 0
    while index < len(segment) and ENV_ASSIGN.match(segment[index]):
        index += 1
    return segment[index:]

def output_is_bounded(command: str, commands: list[list[str]]) -> bool:
    if ">" in command:
        return True
    last = commands[-1]
    if not last:
        return False
    return Path(last[0]).name in BOUNDING_PAGERS

def uses_unbounded_workspace_cargo(command: str, commands: list[list[str]]) -> bool:
    cargo = next(
        (
            argv for argv in commands
            if Path(argv[0]).name == "cargo"
            and len(argv) >= 2
            and argv[1] in CARGO_NOISY
            and "--workspace" in argv
        ),
        None,
    )
    if cargo is None:
        return False
    return not output_is_bounded(command, commands)
```

```python
    assert uses_unbounded_workspace_cargo("cargo test --workspace > /tmp/log", [["cargo", "test", "--workspace"]]) is False
```

**RULE**:
All external hyperlinks in documentation, READMEs, and knowledge bases **MUST** use the `https://` protocol. **MUST NOT** use `http://` for any external resource, regardless of whether the target site supports HTTP.

**WHY**:
1.  **Security:** `http://` links are vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks. If a user clicks an `http` link, their browser may downgrade a secure session or expose credentials if the target site redirects improperly.
2.  **Browser Deprecation:** Modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) flag `http://` sites as "Not Secure," causing user trust erosion and potential blocking of mixed content if the documentation is served over HTTPS.
3.  **Forensic Evidence:** Commit `99ab3bc4` explicitly upgraded `http://www.reactiflux.com/` and `http://creativecommons.org/` to `https://`, confirming this is a mandatory maintenance invariant.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
*   Any Markdown documentation, README, or wiki page.
*   Any configuration file containing external URLs.
*   Any codebase where external resources are referenced via string literals.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```markdown
<!-- CORRECT: Secure Protocol -->
- [React Official Website](https://react.dev/)
- [Creative Commons License](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

<!-- INCORRECT: Insecure Protocol -->
- [React Official Website](http://react.dev/)
- [Creative Commons License](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```markdown
<!-- ANTI-PATTERN: Never use http:// for external links -->
- [Reactiflux Discord Channel](http://www.reactiflux.com/)
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
*   **Linting Rule:** Use a Markdown linter (e.g., `markdownlint` with custom rules or `remark-lint`) to flag any `http://` URLs.
*   **CI Check:** A simple grep command in CI: `grep -r "http://" README.md` should return no results (exit code 1).
*   **Manual Review:** Maintainers must reject PRs containing `http://` links.

2.  **Consistency:** Mixed casing (e.g., "Markstream" vs "markstream") creates cognitive dissonance and suggests a lack of rigor.
3.  **Forensic Evidence:** Commit `c3fdc124` fixed "Markstream" to "markstream" to align with the repository slug `Simon-He95/markstream-vue`. This indicates a strict adherence to canonical naming.

## 3053. Invariant Separation of Async Action Triggers from Popover/Modal Destruction Lifecycle (Harvested from cosscom/ui)

<!-- PROVENANCE_START
{
  "knowledge_type": "engineering_pattern",

}
PROVENANCE_END -->
> **Provenance**: Harvested from [cosscom/ui](https://github.com/cosscom/ui) (Revision: `7f7cbd0e`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
Components that trigger asynchronous mutations or downstream confirmation dialogs MUST NOT be rendered as children of self-dismissing popups/menus, and MUST NOT use immediate-dismiss trigger primitives (`AlertDialogClose`, `DialogClose`, `PopoverClose`) for unsettled asynchronous mutations.

**WHY**:
When an action is initiated from within an unmanaged popup (such as `MenuPopup` or `PopoverPopup`), clicking a menu item executes default dismiss mechanics: the popup unmounts immediately. If an asynchronous mutation is running, the unmounting destroys the local component tree, cancels in-flight state tracking, swallows error handling boundaries, and detaches toast/notification triggers. Furthermore, nesting a confirmation `AlertDialog` inside a `MenuPopup` causes the dialog to instantly unmount the moment the trigger is clicked.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Applies to any menu, dropdown, context menu, drawer menu, or confirmation dialog handling mutating async actions (deletions, network updates, webhooks) across React, Next.js, and Base UI/Radix applications.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```tsx
import * as React from "react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Menu, MenuTrigger, MenuPopup, MenuItem, MenuSeparator } from "@/components/ui/menu";
import { AlertDialog, AlertDialogPopup, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogClose } from "@/components/ui/alert-dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";

export function SafeDestructiveMenuAction({
  onDeleteAsync,
}: {
  onDeleteAsync: () => Promise<void>;
}) {
  const [confirmOpen, setConfirmOpen] = useState(false);
  const [isPending, setIsPending] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  async function handleConfirmDelete() {
    setIsPending(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await onDeleteAsync();
      setConfirmOpen(false); // Only dismiss on verified success
    } catch (err) {
      // Retain modal state to allow retry; display contextual fault
      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Mutation failed");
    } finally {
      setIsPending(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <>
      <Menu>
        <MenuTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" />}>
          Options
        </MenuTrigger>
        <MenuPopup align="end">
          <MenuItem>Edit</MenuItem>
          <MenuSeparator />
          {/* Menu item only sets sibling state; does not render modal inside */}
          <MenuItem onClick={() => setConfirmOpen(true)} variant="destructive">
            Delete
          </MenuItem>
        </MenuPopup>
      </Menu>

      {/* AlertDialog is a controlled SIBLING, surviving Menu teardown */}
      <AlertDialog open={confirmOpen} onOpenChange={setConfirmOpen}>
        <AlertDialogPopup>
          <AlertDialogHeader>
            <AlertDialogTitle>Are you absolutely sure?</AlertDialogTitle>
            <AlertDialogDescription>
              This action cannot be undone.
              {error && <span className="block text-destructive mt-2">{error}</span>}
            </AlertDialogDescription>
          </AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogFooter>
            {/* Cancel uses immediate close */}
            <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="ghost" disabled={isPending} />}>
              Cancel
            </AlertDialogClose>
            {/* Confirm is an isolated, async-managed button - NOT AlertDialogClose */}
            <Button
              variant="destructive"
              loading={isPending}
              onClick={handleConfirmDelete}
            >
              Confirm Deletion
            </Button>
          </AlertDialogFooter>
        </AlertDialogPopup>
      </AlertDialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```tsx
// ANTI-PATTERN: NEVER nest AlertDialog inside MenuPopup or wrap async confirm in AlertDialogClose
<MenuPopup>
  <MenuItem>
    {/* FATAL: Clicking this closes MenuPopup, destroying the AlertDialog mounted inside */}
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Delete</AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogPopup>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          {/* FATAL: AlertDialogClose unmounts dialog before deleteAccount resolves */}
          <AlertDialogClose onClick={() => deleteAccount()}>
            Confirm
          </AlertDialogClose>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogPopup>
    </AlertDialog>
  </MenuItem>
</MenuPopup>
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Run an integration test with React Testing Library verifying that throwing an error during the network request prevents modal unmounting and renders the error message:
```tsx
it("retains alert dialog mounted and shows error when async mutation rejects", async () => {
  const failingMutation = vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error("Server error"));
  render(<SafeDestructiveMenuAction onDeleteAsync={failingMutation} />);
  
  await userEvent.click(screen.getByText("Options"));
  await userEvent.click(screen.getByText("Delete"));
  expect(screen.getByRole("alertdialog")).toBeInTheDocument();
  
  await userEvent.click(screen.getByText("Confirm Deletion"));
  expect(failingMutation).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  // Invariant: Must remain mounted
  expect(screen.getByRole("alertdialog")).toBeInTheDocument();
  expect(screen.getByText("Server error")).toBeInTheDocument();
});
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [cosscom/ui](https://github.com/cosscom/ui) (Revision: `7f7cbd0e`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
Whenever an interactive component computes spatial offsets, sliding transitions, or origin anchor scalings along the X-axis using CSS transforms (`translateX`, `origin-*`), developers MUST implement explicit Right-To-Left (`rtl:`) mirroring overrides for both the sign of the translation vector and the horizontal transform-origin anchors.

**WHY**:
Unlike CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, `inset-inline-start`) which the browser's layout engine automatically mirrors in RTL mode (`dir="rtl"`), CSS transforms operate on the physical Cartesian coordinate system. `translateX(12px)` moves an element to the physical right in both LTR and RTL. In RTL layouts, a switch toggle thumb or sliding drawer translating with positive physical coordinates slides *out* of its bounding track container and overflows into adjacent DOM nodes. Additionally, asymmetric scale animations (`scale-x-110`) anchored to `origin-left` distort in the opposite direction of movement.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All switch components, animated slider thumbs, sliding segment indicators, collapsible side panels, and swipe-gesture visual indicators.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```tsx
// Concrete token-level invariant from cosscom/ui Switch and MenuCheckboxItem
export function MirroredSwitchThumb() {
  return (
    <span
      className={cn(
        "pointer-events-none block aspect-square h-full",
        // LTR defaults
        "origin-left",
        "data-checked:origin-[var(--thumb-size)_50%]",
        "data-checked:translate-x-[calc(var(--thumb-size)-4px)]",
        // Press scale mechanics
        "in-[[role=switch]:active]:scale-x-110",
        // RTL overrides: invert origin and reverse translate-x sign
        "rtl:origin-right",
        "rtl:data-checked:origin-left",
        "rtl:data-checked:-translate-x-[calc(var(--thumb-size)-4px)]"
      )}
    />
  );
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```tsx
// ANTI-PATTERN: Relying strictly on physical transform without RTL inversion
<span
  className={cn(
    "origin-left",
    "data-checked:translate-x-[calc(var(--thumb-size)-4px)]"
    // Missing rtl: - In RTL, thumb tracks away from background pill and overflows
  )}
/>
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Validate via visual regression snapshot test under both `dir="ltr"` and `dir="rtl"` modes or AST style lint:
```bash
# Automated assertion in Playwright
await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir', 'rtl'));
const thumbBox = await page.locator('[data-slot="switch-thumb"]').boundingBox();
const trackBox = await page.locator('[data-slot="switch"]').boundingBox();
expect(thumbBox.x).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(trackBox.x);
expect(thumbBox.x + thumbBox.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(trackBox.x + trackBox.width);
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [cosscom/ui](https://github.com/cosscom/ui) (Revision: `7f7cbd0e`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
When integrating controlled schema validation libraries (such as React Hook Form with Zod/Valibot) with form input wrappers (`Field`), the developer MUST declare `<form noValidate>` and MUST NOT attach native constraint attributes (`required`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`) to underlying HTML input controls unless explicitly bypassing the schema resolver.

**WHY**:
Modern design-system primitives (such as Base UI `Field`) automatically subscribe to the native DOM `ValidityState` of wrapped inputs. If an `<input required type="email" />` is declared inside a React Hook Form flow, the browser or Base UI constraint validator intercepts the form submit event *before* React Hook Form's `handleSubmit` callback fires. The native handler suppresses submit, exhibits browser-dependent tooltip validation bubbles, and prevents user-space error presentation hooks (`FieldError`, Zod schema refinement, toast notifications) from executing.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All client-side form architectures where external validation schemas manage form validity state.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```tsx
import * as React from "react";
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
import { z } from "zod";
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription, FieldError } from "@/components/ui/field";
import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input";

const schema = z.object({
  email: z.string().min(1, "Email is required").email("Invalid email address"),
});

type FormValues = z.infer<typeof schema>;

export function ValidatedForm() {
  const {
    register,
    handleSubmit,
    formState: { errors },
  } = useForm<FormValues>({
    resolver: zodResolver(schema),
  });

  return (
    // Invariant: noValidate prevents native browser interception
    <form noValidate onSubmit={handleSubmit((data) => console.log(data))}>
      <Field invalid={Boolean(errors.email)} name="email">
        <FieldLabel>
          Email <span className="text-destructive-foreground">*</span>
        </FieldLabel>
        {/*
          Invariant: Do NOT add 'required'.
          Keep type="email" for mobile virtual keyboard or use inputMode="email"
        */}
        <Input
          type="email"
          placeholder="user@example.com"
          {...register("email")}
        />
        <FieldDescription>We will send account alerts here.</FieldDescription>
        <FieldError>{errors.email?.message}</FieldError>
      </Field>
    </form>
  );
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```tsx
// ANTI-PATTERN: Native constraint attributes conflict with schema validation library
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>
  {/* BUG: required and type="email" trigger native bubble; RHF resolver never runs */}
  <Field name="email">
    <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
    <Input required type="email" {...register("email")} />
    <FieldError>{errors.email?.message}</FieldError>
  </Field>
</form>
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:
Unit test verifying form submit failure without native tooltip interference:
```tsx
it("triggers schema error without triggering HTML5 checkValidity interception", async () => {
  render(<ValidatedForm />);
  const submitButton = screen.getByRole("button", { name: /submit/i });
  await userEvent.click(submitButton);
  expect(await screen.findByText("Email is required")).toBeInTheDocument();
});
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [ratatui/ratatui](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui) (Revision: `c27a3cf1`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
In immediate-mode user interface architectures, widgets MUST NOT encapsulate mutable temporal runtime state inside the rendering struct itself. Systems MUST split components into an immutable or zero-sized rendering descriptor (`Widget`) and an explicitly typed, independently mutable lifecycle struct (`StatefulWidget::State`).

**WHY**:
Encapsulating mutable runtime state within the rendering object forces the top-level view rendering tree to hold exclusive mutable references (`&mut Self`). In recursive hierarchies or split views, this causes borrow-checker deadlocks, prevents concurrent rendering of distinct subviews, and prohibits pure visual property testing without instantiating complex operational state. Separating state allows the renderer to remain a pure, stateless projection over an arbitrary external buffer.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to all terminal, canvas, immediate-mode GUI, and game rendering loops where state spans multiple frames (e.g., scroll offsets, selected indices, cache trees, text input cursors).

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```rust
use ratatui::buffer::Buffer;
use ratatui::layout::Rect;
use ratatui::widgets::{StatefulWidget, Widget};

// 1. Pure stateless render descriptor (can be zero-sized or configuration only)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct TableRenderer {
    pub show_headers: bool,
}

// 2. Pure runtime mutable state
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct TableRuntimeState {
    pub selected_row: usize,
    pub scroll_offset: usize,
}

impl TableRuntimeState {
    pub const fn select_next(&mut self, total_items: usize) {
        if total_items == 0 {
            self.selected_row = 0;
            return;
        }
        self.selected_row = (self.selected_row + 1).min(total_items - 1);
    }
}

// 3. Trait implementation connecting descriptor and state via disjoint references
impl StatefulWidget for TableRenderer {
    type State = TableRuntimeState;

    fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, state: &mut Self::State) {
        // Safe: self is consumed by value or borrowed immutably;
        // state is exclusively borrowed only within this local frame scope.
        if area.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        let display_row = state.selected_row.saturating_sub(state.scroll_offset);
        let target_y = area.y.saturating_add(display_row as u16);
        if target_y < area.bottom() {
            buf.set_string(
                area.x,
                target_y,
                format!("Row {}", state.selected_row),
                ratatui::style::Style::default(),
            );
        }
    }
}
```

**RULE**:
Any application capturing terminal raw mode, alternate screen buffers, or mouse capture flags MUST encapsulate terminal lifecycle setup and teardown within an RAII guard or centralized unwind boundary (`catch_unwind` / hook). The application MUST NOT exit or panic while leaving the terminal in raw unbuffered mode.

**WHY**:
Entering raw mode disables standard OS-level line buffering, local echo, and signal handling (`SIGINT` translation to `0x03`). If a panic or early return occurs without executing `crossterm::terminal::disable_raw_mode()` and `LeaveAlternateScreen`, the user's host shell is left completely corrupted (invisible input, disabled echo, broken newline offsets, hung cursor).

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Mandatory for all CLI/TUI programs in Rust, C, C++, Go, or Python interacting with POSIX `termios` or Windows Console input modes.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```rust
use std::io::{self, stdout, Stdout};
use crossterm::{
    execute,
    terminal::{disable_raw_mode, enable_raw_mode, EnterAlternateScreen, LeaveAlternateScreen},
};

pub struct TerminalGuard {
    _private: (),
}

impl TerminalGuard {
    pub fn init() -> io::Result<Self> {
        enable_raw_mode()?;
        let mut out = stdout();
        execute!(out, EnterAlternateScreen)?;
        
        // Install panic hook that guarantees cleanup before stack trace is printed
        let original_hook = std::panic::take_hook();
        std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |panic_info| {
            let _ = Self::cleanup_terminal();
            original_hook(panic_info);
        }));

        Ok(Self { _private: () })
    }

    fn cleanup_terminal() -> io::Result<()> {
        let mut out = stdout();
        execute!(out, LeaveAlternateScreen)?;
        disable_raw_mode()?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Drop for TerminalGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = Self::cleanup_terminal();
    }
}

// Canonical usage:
pub fn safe_tui_entrypoint<F>(logic: F) -> io::Result<()>
where
    F: FnOnce() -> io::Result<()>,
{
    let _guard = TerminalGuard::init()?;
    logic()
    // _guard drops automatically on normal exit, ? return, or panic unwind
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```rust

// Any `?` or panic between enable and disable permanently bricks the user's terminal session.

    enable_raw_mode()?; // Terminal corrupted from here
    let mut out = stdout();
    execute!(out, EnterAlternateScreen)?;

    let result = risky_operation_that_might_panic()?; // <-- PANIC LEAVES SHELL BROKEN!

    execute!(out, LeaveAlternateScreen)?;
    disable_raw_mode()?;
    Ok(())
}
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [angular/angular](https://github.com/angular/angular) (Revision: `fdb84e2e`).  
> **Evidence**: Verified against commit diffs and closed defect autopsies. (Distillation Prohibited).

**RULE**:
Any synchronous dispatcher MUST iterate over an immutable snapshot or defensive clone of listener registries. Dispatchers MUST NOT iterate directly over mutable collections when listeners can synchronously mutate (subscribe/unsubscribe) the registry during emission.

**WHY**:
When an event listener invokes an unsubscription routine synchronously (e.g., RxJS `take(1)`, self-deregistering callbacks, or disposal hooks), mutating an in-place collection (such as `listeners.splice(index, 1)`) shifts subsequent listener elements leftward. In an ongoing forward traversal (`for (let i = 0; i < listeners.length; i++)`), index incrementation causes the iterator to skip the immediate next subscriber, causing silent data drops.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Apply to any observable pattern, callback queue, reactive notifier, webhook trigger, or event emitter in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go where listener execution is synchronous.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
export class SafeEventEmitter<T> {
  private listeners: Array<(value: T) => void> = [];
  private isEmitting = false;

  subscribe(listener: (value: T) => void): () => void {
    this.listeners.push(listener);
    return () => {
      if (this.isEmitting) {
        // Copy-on-write during dispatch prevents mutating the active iteration frame
        this.listeners = this.listeners.filter((l) => l !== listener);
      } else {
        const index = this.listeners.indexOf(listener);
        if (index !== -1) {
          this.listeners.splice(index, 1);
        }
      }
    };
  }

  emit(value: T): void {
    this.isEmitting = true;
    // Snapshot subscriber list to freeze active dispatch slice
    const snapshot = this.listeners.slice();
    try {
      for (let i = 0; i < snapshot.length; i++) {
        // Guard against handlers that were unsubscribed earlier in the same cycle
        if (this.listeners.includes(snapshot[i])) {
          snapshot[i](value);
        }
      }
    } finally {
      this.isEmitting = false;
    }
  }
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript
// ANTI-PATTERN: Iterating directly over mutable array while invoking arbitrary callbacks
export class VulnerableEmitter<T> {
  private listeners: Array<(value: T) => void> = [];

  emit(value: T): void {
    // If listener 0 calls unsubscribe(), listeners[1] moves to index 0.
    // Loop increments i to 1, completely skipping the new index 0!
    for (let i = 0; i < this.listeners.length; i++) {
      this.listeners[i](value);
    }
  }
}
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:

```typescript
    delivered.push(`l1:${val}`);

    delivered.push(`l2:${val}`);
```

**RULE**:
Static analysis compilers and AST visitors parsing external user input MUST NOT invoke panics (`unreachable!()`, `panic!()`, or unexpected crashes) on syntax/expression variants that are syntactically valid in the host language. All unrecognized or malformed AST nodes MUST map to explicit semantic compiler diagnostics.

**WHY**:
In TypeScript/JavaScript, spread elements (`...expr`), computed properties, or dynamic calls are valid AST nodes. If a decorator or macro parser expects an `ObjectExpression` and asserts `Argument::as_expression().unwrap()`, or classifies spreads as `unreachable!()`, user code containing spreads crashes the compiler process instead of producing a diagnostics report with file coordinates.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Static analysis frameworks, AST transformers, Babel plugins, Rust OXC/SWC plugins, and language servers analyzing TypeScript, Rust, or Python ASTs.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```rust
// Verified Rust OXC AST traversal matching
pub fn parse_options_literal<'a>(
    arg: Option<&oxc_ast::ast::Argument<'a>>,
    issues: &mut Vec<ValueIssue>,
) -> Option<&'a oxc_ast::ast::ObjectExpression<'a>> {
    let arg = arg?;
    
    // Explicitly destructure AST variant instead of unchecked unwrapping
    match arg {
        oxc_ast::ast::Argument::SpreadElement(spread) => {
            issues.push(ValueIssue::new(
                "NG1001",
                spread.span,
                "Spread expressions are not supported in compile-time metadata configurations.".to_string(),
            ));
            None
        }
        _ => match arg.as_expression() {
            Some(oxc_ast::ast::Expression::ObjectExpression(obj)) => Some(obj),
            Some(expr) => {
                issues.push(ValueIssue::wrong_type(
                    expr.span(),
                    "Argument needs to be an object literal that is statically analyzable.",
                ));
                None
            }
            None => {
                issues.push(ValueIssue::arg_not_literal(
                    arg.span(),
                    "Argument must evaluate to an expression literal.",
                ));
                None
            }
        },
    }
}
```

**RULE**:
When rendering standard markup trees (e.g., CommonMark/HTML), attributes reflecting sequence indices (such as `<ol start="...">`) MUST be emitted if and only if the sequence offset deviates from the canonical baseline (`start !== 1`), while rejecting false-positive omissions caused by empty-string token falsity.

**WHY**:
Markdown parsers (such as `marked`) parse list tokens and emit list segments. When a numbered list is interrupted by arbitrary block tokens (code blocks, blockquotes, images) and resumes at index 3, emitting `<ol>` without `start="3"` resets numbering in the browser DOM to 1. Omitting the start attribute when `start === 1` maintains canonical HTML cleanliness, but evaluating `start !== 1 && start !== ''` is required to eliminate empty or invalid string serialization.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Static site generators, documentation AST pipelines, CMS Markdown-to-HTML transformers, and custom CommonMark renderers.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```typescript
import { Renderer, Tokens } from 'marked';

export function listRender(this: Renderer, token: Tokens.List): string {
  const { items, ordered, start } = token;
  if (ordered) {
    // Only emit the attribute if start is explicitly provided and non-canonical
    const hasCustomStart = start !== undefined && start !== 1 && start !== '';
    const startAttribute = hasCustomStart ? ` start="${encodeURIComponent(String(start))}"` : '';
    return `<ol class="docs-ordered-list"${startAttribute}>\n${items.map(item => this.listitem(item)).join('')}\n</ol>\n`;
  }
  return `<ul class="docs-unordered-list">\n${items.map(item => this.listitem(item)).join('')}\n</ul>\n`;
}
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```typescript

  return `<ul>${items.map(i => this.listitem(i)).join('')}</ul>`;
```

**RULE**:
When inspecting callable type annotations in dependency injection engines, you MUST verify that an inspected parameter's annotation is an instance of `type` before passing it to `issubclass()`. You MUST NOT evaluate `typing.Union`, `typing.Annotated`, type variables, or unparameterized forms with `issubclass()`.

**WHY**:
Third-party wrappers and framework callbacks (such as Twisted `Deferred.callback` in `scrapy shell`) often declare signatures typed with unions (e.g., `Union[_DeferredResultT, Failure]`) or custom callables. Invoking `issubclass(annotation, TargetClass)` when `annotation` is a `typing._SpecialForm` or `typing.Union` raises a fatal `TypeError: issubclass() arg 1 must be a class` at runtime, causing silent failure masking inside event loops.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
Any Python runtime dependency injection, reflection engine, or RPC serialization framework that extracts type annotations from arbitrary functions or methods dynamically.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
import inspect
from typing import Any, get_origin, Union

def is_safe_subclass(annotation: Any, target_class: type) -> bool:
    """
    Safely determine if an annotation is a subclass of target_class,
    guarding against typing constructs, SpecialForms, and Union types.
    """
    # Strip optional/annotated metadata wrappers if necessary
    origin = get_origin(annotation)
    if origin is not None:
        # Handles generic aliases like list[str], type[Foo]
        if isinstance(origin, type) and issubclass(origin, target_class):
            return True
        return False

    # Annotation must be an explicit instance of `type`
    if not isinstance(annotation, type):
        return False

    return issubclass(annotation, target_class)

def extract_injectable_parameters(func: Any, target_base: type) -> list[str]:
    signature = inspect.signature(func)
    injectable_args: list[str] = []
    
    for param_name, param in signature.parameters.items():
        if param.annotation is inspect.Parameter.empty:
            continue
            
        if is_safe_subclass(param.annotation, target_base):
            injectable_args.append(param_name)
            
    return injectable_args
```

**NEGATIVE CONSTRAINT**:
```python
# ANTI-PATTERN: Direct issubclass check on function parameter annotations
import inspect

def bad_extract_parameters(func, target_base):
    sig = inspect.signature(func)
    # Crashes on Union[A, B], Any, Callable, or Twisted Failure annotations!
    return [
        name for name, p in sig.parameters.items()
        if p.annotation is not inspect.Parameter.empty 
        and issubclass(p.annotation, target_base)  # TypeError: issubclass() arg 1 must be a class
    ]
```

**VERIFICATION METHOD**:

```python

    def callback_with_union(x: int | str, y: Any, z: type): pass
    assert extract_injectable_parameters(callback_with_union, object) == ["z"]
```

> **Provenance**: Harvested from [scrapinghub/scrapy-poet](https://github.com/scrapinghub/scrapy-poet) (Revision: `f06d684b`).

**RULE**:
When running out-of-process network test harnesses (mock HTTP servers) within asynchronous test runners, the parent process MUST block on an explicit stdout sync token emitted by the subprocess *after* socket binding before executing client requests, and the subprocess shutdown MUST hook `SIGTERM` handlers to guarantee coverage measurement recording.

**WHY**:
Spawning a server subprocess via `Popen` and immediately querying the TCP port introduces a Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU) race condition: the port may be allocated via ephemeral bind, but the server reactor is not yet in its listen state. Merely checking port availability causes intermittent `ConnectionRefusedError`. Furthermore, terminating mock subprocesses abruptly without SIGTERM capture (`coverage.run sigterm = true`) results in unwritten `.coverage` files and distorted code coverage metrics.

**WHEN TO APPLY**:
All integration testing frameworks where Twisted, Tornado, Node.js, or Go subprocesses act as local fixture servers for network protocol clients.

**VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN**:
```python
import os
import socket
import sys
from subprocess import PIPE, Popen
from types import TracebackType
from typing import Self

def get_ephemeral_port() -> int:
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
        s.bind(("", 0))
        return int(s.getsockname()[1])

class SynchronousSubprocessHarness:
    def __init__(self, resource_target: str) -> None:
        self.resource_target = resource_target
        self.port = get_ephemeral_port()
        self.proc: Popen[bytes] | None = None
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}"

    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
        # Pass -u for unbuffered binary stdout
        self.proc = Popen(
            [
                sys.executable,
                "-u",
                "-m",
                "harness_runner",
                self.resource_target,
                "--port",
                str(self.port),
            ],
            stdout=PIPE,
            stderr=PIPE,
            env={**os.environ},
        )
        assert self.proc.stdout is not None, "Subprocess stdout pipe allocation failed"
        
        # SYNCHRONIZATION BARRIER:
        # Blocks parent process until child emits the newline confirming reactor is listening
        sync_line = self.proc.stdout.readline()
        if not sync_line or b"READY" not in sync_line:
            err = self.proc.stderr.read().decode() if self.proc.stderr else ""
            raise RuntimeError(f"Server harness failed initialization: {err}")
            
        return self

    def __exit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc_val: BaseException | None,
        exc_tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        if self.proc:
            # Terminate sends SIGTERM allowing tool.coverage to flush profiles
            self.proc.terminate()
            self.proc.wait(timeout=5)
```

Child subprocess implementation:
```python
# Child process setup
from twisted.internet import reactor
from twisted.web.server import Site

def launch_server(resource, port: int) -> None:
    factory = Site(resource)
    reactor.listenTCP(port, factory)
    
    def on_reactor_running() -> None:
        # Emits synchronization token strictly after reactor is accepting connections
        sys.stdout.write(f"READY port={port}\n")
        sys.stdout.flush()

    reactor.callWhenRunning(on_reactor_running)
    reactor.run()
```

```python
        time.sleep(0.5)  # FLAKY: Subject to CPU scheduling jitter, triggers ConnectionRefused
        return self
```
